subject: Throughput sizing post-call: follow-up & data request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alan Chu <alan.chu@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:23-07:00
Subject: Throughput sizing post-call: follow-up & data request

Thanks for the call this morning, Alan — great discussion. Quick recap and a short list of inputs we need to run a first-pass throughput and cost sizing for your production workload.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: live customer support assistant (web + mobile).
- Typical conversation pattern: 1 user message -> 1 streamed model response (we stream partial tokens to UI).
- Current traffic: peaks during 09:00–11:00 PT and 17:00–19:00 PT.

Data we need from you to size throughput / SLO:
1) Average tokens per request (input + model output) — if you can split input vs output that helps.
2) Expected peak QPS (requests/sec) and steady-state QPS.
3) Concurrency (simultaneous open sessions) and how it maps to QPS.
4) Desired latency SLOs (eg. p50/p95/p99 for first byte and for final token).
5) Streaming requirements: are you streaming every token as it’s produced (low-latency streaming) or only periodically? Protocol (SSE / WebSocket / chunked HTTP)?
6) Any hard constraints on cost or preferred model family (open vs proprietary).

Next steps from our side:
- If you can share a small sampling spreadsheet (token distribution by percentiles, QPS by hour) we’ll load it into our sizing model and return a recommended config and estimated cost/latency tradeoffs.
- I’ve attached a one-page template (finex_workload_summary.xlsx) you can fill; Rafael will run the model once we have it.

Could you please fill the attached sheet and return by EOD Friday? If easier, we can take a short follow-up call to walk through the fields.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0104

Attachments: finex_workload_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet template)

From: Alan Chu <alan.chu@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Finex Ops <ops@finex.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T14:05:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: follow-up & data request

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers inline below and I attached a rough export from our telemetry.

1) Avg tokens per request: input ~40 tokens, model output ~170 tokens, so ~210 total on average.
2) QPS: steady-state ~420 QPS, typical weekday peak ~1,600 QPS (we see short bursts up to ~2,400 QPS for 2–3 minutes during events).
3) Concurrency: we typically have ~3,200 open sessions during peak, but only ~1,100 actively generating requests at any given second.
4) Latency SLOs: client expectation is first-byte <200ms p95 and final token p95 <400ms. We track p99 as well and want it <700ms if possible.
5) Streaming: yes, client apps stream tokens via WebSocket; we prefer token-by-token streaming (low-latency).
6) Cost: we’re cost sensitive — target is to keep monthly inference spend under $45k if feasible.

Attached: finex_telemetry_sample.csv (note: anonymized). I’ll try to fill your template but the telemetry export should be enough to run an initial model.

—Alan
Alan Chu
VP Product, Finex
alan.chu@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Alan Chu <alan.chu@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T10:22:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: follow-up & data request

Thanks for the data, Alan — this is very helpful. Quick notes based on those numbers and next steps: 

Initial sizing observations:
- At 210 tokens/request and 1,600 QPS peak -> ~336k tokens/sec peak. Steady-state (420 QPS) -> ~88.2k tokens/sec.
- With token-by-token streaming, per-request latency is dominated by model generation & per-token dispatch. For p95 first-byte <200ms we’ll want to ensure a low-latency model variant and an instance count that avoids queuing.
- Concurrency mapping: your 1,100 active generators at peak matches ~1,600 QPS (users doing ~1.45 requests/sec on average); we'll use that to size pooling/batching.

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ll run our sizing model with two candidate families: an optimized 7B quantized variant (best cost/throughput) and a 13B low-latency variant (better tail latency).
2) I need the telemetry sample (Alan’s attachment) in XLSX or CSV format; I’ve attached our sizing workbook (redwood_sizing_model_v1.xlsx) — please either paste the sample into the ‘Input’ tab or drop a shared link.
3) I’ll produce an output that includes: estimated GPUs required (type + count), expected p50/p95/p99 latencies at the model and network layers, estimated tokens/sec capacity per pooled instance, and a cost estimate for hosted vs. dedicated (monthly).

Questions for Alan:
- For the p99 target you mentioned (<700ms), is that aligned to a business requirement or just an internal goal? If it’s business-critical we should size for it.
- How tolerant is the UX to a model-fallback strategy (eg. degrade to a smaller model during sustained bursts)?

I’ll aim to run the workbook tomorrow and share a draft recommendation by EOD Friday.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_sizing_model_v1.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alan Chu <alan.chu@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-17T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing post-call: follow-up & data request

Perfect — thanks both. Alan, if you can drop the telemetry CSV into the shared Drive link (or reply with the XLSX) I’ll confirm Rafael has access and we’ll lock a 30-min follow-up for Monday to review the sizing outputs.

Proposed agenda for the follow-up call (30 min):
- Walk through the sizing outputs (GPU count, expected p95/p99 latencies)
- Discuss fallback & routing policy (smaller model vs. queueing)
- Outline Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoffs and SLA implications
- Agree on next steps and an internal playbook for capacity scaling during special events

Proposed time: Monday 2026-07-20 09:00–09:30 PT — does that work? If not, propose two alternatives.

Thanks,
Neha
